Name: Reimbursement of financing costs incurred by nonprofit contractors due to city-controlled delays.
Title: A Local Law to amend the administrative code of the city of New York, in relation to reimbursement of financing costs incurred by nonprofit contractors due to city-controlled delays

History.Description: This Introduction was Introduced by Council
This Introduction was Referred to Comm by Council to the Committee on Contracts

Summary: This bill would require contracting agencies to reimburse nonprofit contractors for interest and lender fees on loans or lines of credit used to keep providing services while a City contract awaits registration by the Comptroller, including costs treated as indirect costs under the City’s human services cost manual. The delay would run from the later of the contract start date or 30 days after the contractor submits all registration documents. Contractors could submit claims to the contracting agency within 180 days after the delay ends, and reimbursement would be paid in addition to the contract amount. The City Chief Procurement Officer would report annually on claims, including how many are approved or denied. The bill would apply to contracts entered into, renewed, extended, or amended on or after its effective date.
Text:
A Local Law to amend the administrative code of the city of New York, in relation to reimbursement of financing costs incurred by nonprofit contractors due to city-controlled delays

Be it enacted by the Council as follows:


 Section 1. Chapter 1 of title 6 of the administrative code of the city of New York is amended by adding a new section 6-152 to read as follows:
§ 6-152 Reimbursement of financing costs incurred due to city-controlled delays. a. Definitions. For the purposes of this section, the following terms have the following meanings:
City-controlled delay. The term “city-controlled delay” means the period beginning on the start date of a covered contract, or 30 days after the date on which a nonprofit contractor submits to the contracting agency all documentation required for the registration of such contract, whichever is later, and ending on the date on which such contract is registered by the comptroller. Such term does not include any period during which the contracting agency or comptroller is awaiting additional documentation from such nonprofit contractor.
Covered contract. The term “covered contract” means a contract for services between a contracting agency and a nonprofit contractor that is entered into, renewed, extended, or amended on or after the effective date of the local law that added this section.
Eligible financing costs. The term “eligible financing costs” means reasonable interest and lender fees incurred by a nonprofit contractor on a loan or line of credit from a bank, credit union, community development financial institution, or other lender authorized by law, the proceeds of which are used for payroll and employee benefits, rent, insurance, utilities, or other costs incurred in the performance of a covered contract during a city-controlled delay. Such term does not include principal, late charges, default interest, prepayment penalties, or any other charge arising from a nonprofit contractor’s breach of a financing agreement.
Eligible indirect costs. The term “eligible indirect costs” means eligible financing costs that are indirect costs as determined in accordance with the health and human services cost policies and procedures manual.
Health and human services cost policies and procedures manual. The term “health and human services cost policies and procedures manual” means the New York city health and human services cost policies and procedures manual, or any successor manual governing the allocation of costs under human services contracts.
Nonprofit contractor. The term “nonprofit contractor” means a not-for-profit corporation that is exempt from federal income taxation pursuant to section 501(c)(3) of the internal revenue code and is a party to a contract with a contracting agency.
b. The applicable contracting agency shall reimburse a nonprofit contractor for eligible financing costs, including eligible indirect costs, incurred due to a city-controlled delay. Such reimbursement shall be limited to eligible financing costs, including eligible indirect costs, attributable to amounts payable under a covered contract for services provided and costs incurred during such city-controlled delay and shall be in addition to the amount of such contract. A contracting agency shall not reduce any award, payment, or advance payment to a nonprofit contractor because such contractor becomes eligible for reimbursement pursuant to this section.
c. A nonprofit contractor may submit a claim for reimbursement for eligible financing costs, including eligible indirect costs, to the contracting agency for up to 180 days after the end of the city-controlled delay. Such claim shall include documentation of the city-controlled delay, the interest and fees incurred, and the use of such financing in support of a covered contract.
d. No later than October 1, 2027, and annually thereafter, the city chief procurement officer shall submit to the speaker of the council and post on the website of the mayor’s office of contract services a report regarding claims for reimbursement submitted pursuant to this section during the preceding fiscal year. Such report shall include, at minimum:
1. The number of claims received, how many such claims are approved, denied, or partially approved;
2. The total amount of reimbursements paid, disaggregated by contracting agency; and
3. Any other information determined to be relevant by the city chief procurement officer.
§ 2. This local law takes effect 180 days after it becomes law.
